overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 2
overview.text: This lesson asks students to use the first steps in the modeling cycle when a mathematical relationship is represented as a table of values. They look for trends and patterns in the data and formulate a model. First, they look for common differences between the function values of regular intervals (i.e., the first differences for linear and the second differences for quadratic). For exponential functions, they look for a common ratio and/or a constant percent change. For this lesson, all data is based on functions' inputs and outputs, and the numbers are friendly. Throughout this module, refer to the modeling cycle below (found on page 61 of the CCLS and page 72 of the CCSSM):
outcomes: Students recognize linear, quadratic, and exponential functions when presented as a data set or sequence and formulate a model based on the data.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

problems.prompt: If it exists, find the minimum or maximum value for the function model. If there is no minimum or maximum, explain why.
problems.solution:
Since this is an exponential function, the y-values increase as x-values increase, and there is no maximum value. As x gets smaller and smaller (i.e., moves further to the left on the number line), the y-values approach 0 but never reach 0 and never become negative. Therefore, there is no minimum value of this function.
